pool.name: Ackie Monitor
pool.blurb: The ackie monitor (ridge-tailed monitor) is a small, active monitor lizard native to the rocky arid regions of northwestern and central Australia.

pool.name: African Grey Parrot
pool.blurb: The African grey parrot is widely regarded as the most intelligent parrot species and among the most cognitively sophisticated of all animals.

pool.name: Amano Shrimp
pool.blurb: The Amano shrimp is the largest of the dwarf shrimp commonly kept in freshwater aquariums and arguably the single best algae eater in the hobby, tackling hair, thread, and even tough beard algae that most fish and other shrimp ignore.

pool.name: Green Anaconda
pool.blurb: It gives birth to live young, sometimes dozens at a time, rather than laying eggs.

pool.name: Angelfish
pool.blurb: The freshwater angelfish is a cichlid native to the slow-moving tributaries and flooded forest of the Amazon Basin.

pool.name: Green Anole
pool.blurb: The green anole is North America's only native anole and the most commonly kept anole species in captivity.

pool.name: Axolotl
pool.blurb: The axolotl is a neotenic salamander - a species that retains larval features (gills, aquatic lifestyle) permanently throughout its adult life, never undergoing metamorphosis.

pool.name: Aye-Aye
pool.blurb: It fills the ecological role woodpeckers occupy elsewhere. Madagascar has no woodpeckers.

pool.name: Bald Eagle
pool.blurb: It is not bald. The name comes from "balde", an old word for white, describing the head.

pool.name: Ball Python
pool.blurb: The ball python - called the royal python in Europe - is native to the grasslands and open forests of sub-Saharan West and Central Africa.

pool.name: Beagle
pool.blurb: The Beagle descends from small English pack scenthounds bred to trail hare on foot, kept deliberately smaller than mounted hunting hounds so that owners without a horse could keep up.

pool.name: Bearded Dragon
pool.blurb: The inland bearded dragon is native to Australia's arid and semi-arid interior, where it basks on rocks and fence posts in open woodland and scrubland.

pool.name: Bengal
pool.blurb: The Bengal cat is a hybrid breed produced by crossing domestic cats with the Asian leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis), a small wild felid native to South and East Asia.

pool.name: Betta Fish
pool.blurb: The betta fish, or Siamese fighting fish, is native to the shallow rice paddies, floodplains, and slow-moving waters of Southeast Asia.

pool.name: Boa Constrictor
pool.blurb: Boa constrictors are large, heavy-bodied snakes distributed from Mexico through Central and South America to Caribbean island populations.

pool.name: Border Collie
pool.blurb: The border collie is widely considered the most intelligent dog breed in the world, developed on the Anglo-Scottish border specifically for herding sheep using an intense "eye" (predatory stare) and crouching movement.

pool.name: Box Turtle
pool.blurb: Box turtles are North America's most beloved native turtle, found from the eastern United States west to the Great Plains.

pool.name: Budgie / Parakeet
pool.blurb: The budgerigar (budgie) is native to the semi-arid interior of Australia, where enormous nomadic flocks follow rainfall and seed availability across the outback.

pool.name: Bulldog
pool.blurb: The Bulldog was created in medieval England for bull-baiting, and its ancestors were selected for huge jaws and a high pain threshold.

pool.name: Canary
pool.blurb: The domestic canary descends from the wild Atlantic canary, native to the Canary Islands, Azores, and Madeira, and has been selectively bred since the 16th century into distinct song and appearance varieties.

pool.name: Capybara
pool.blurb: It can sleep in water, keeping only its nose above the surface.

pool.name: Cardinal Tetra
pool.blurb: The cardinal tetra is a small schooling fish from the blackwater tributaries of the Amazon and Orinoco basins, closely resembling the neon tetra but with its iridescent red stripe running the full length of the body rather than just the rear half.

pool.name: Veiled Chameleon
pool.blurb: The veiled chameleon is native to the mountainous valleys of Yemen and southwestern Saudi Arabia, where it tolerates wider swings in temperature and humidity than most other chameleon species - an adaptation to its relatively dry, variable habitat.

pool.name: Cherry Shrimp
pool.blurb: The cherry shrimp is one of the most popular freshwater aquarium shrimp species in the hobby, prized for breeding readily in plain freshwater and for the huge range of selectively bred colors developed from a single dull, translucent wild form.

pool.name: Chinchilla
pool.blurb: Chinchillas are native to the high-altitude Andes mountains of South America, where they inhabit rocky terrain at elevations up to 14,000 feet.

pool.name: Clownfish
pool.blurb: The deal runs both ways: the anemone gets cleaned, defended and fed on scraps.

pool.name: Cockatiel
pool.blurb: Cockatiels are the smallest member of the cockatoo family and are endemic to Australia, where they inhabit open country and lightly wooded areas across the continent.

pool.name: Cockatoo
pool.blurb: The umbrella cockatoo, native to the tropical rainforests of Indonesia's Maluku Islands, is one of the most commonly kept cockatoo species and among the most affection-dependent parrots in aviculture.

pool.name: Madagascar Hissing Cockroach
pool.blurb: The Madagascar hissing cockroach is one of the largest cockroach species in the world and the only known hissing insect that produces sound through modified spiracles (breathing pores) rather than wing rubbing.

pool.name: Border Collie
pool.blurb: The border collie is widely considered the most intelligent dog breed in the world, developed on the Anglo-Scottish border specifically for herding sheep using an intense "eye" (predatory stare) and crouching movement.

pool.name: Green Cheek Conure
pool.blurb: Green cheek conures are small parrots native to the forests of Bolivia, Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay, where they live in noisy flocks in the forest canopy.

pool.name: Corn Snake
pool.blurb: Corn snakes are slender, medium-sized rat snakes native to the eastern United States.

pool.name: Corydoras Catfish
pool.blurb: Corydoras catfish are small, armored, bottom-dwelling fish native to the rivers and streams of South America.

pool.name: Crested Gecko
pool.blurb: Native to New Caledonia's southern islands, the crested gecko was thought extinct until rediscovered in 1994.

pool.name: Crow
pool.blurb: Crows that were never trapped will still scold the mask, so the grudge is being passed on.

pool.name: Victoria Crowned Pigeon
pool.blurb: Both parents produce crop milk, so a male pigeon can feed a chick as well as a female.

pool.name: Cuttlefish
pool.blurb: The cuttlebone is a gas-filled internal shell it floods and empties to sink and rise.

pool.name: Dachshund
pool.blurb: Dachshund is German for badger dog, and the breed was built to do exactly that, going to ground after burrowing carnivores.

pool.name: Blue Poison Dart Frog
pool.blurb: Captive-bred individuals are not poisonous, because they never eat the wild arthropods the toxins come from.

pool.name: Degu
pool.blurb: Degus are diurnal rodents from central Chile, and almost everything unusual about them follows from that.

pool.name: Discus
pool.blurb: Discus are tall, laterally compressed cichlids from the slow-moving blackwater tributaries of the Amazon Basin, prized in the aquarium hobby as the self-styled 'king of the aquarium' for their vivid, selectively bred color patterns.

pool.name: Bottlenose Dolphin
pool.blurb: A dolphin will copy another dolphin’s signature whistle to get its attention, which is close to calling someone by name.

pool.name: Bearded Dragon
pool.blurb: The inland bearded dragon is native to Australia's arid and semi-arid interior, where it basks on rocks and fence posts in open woodland and scrubland.

pool.name: African Elephant
pool.blurb: Part of the call travels through the ground, and an elephant can pick it up through its feet.

pool.name: Fennec Fox
pool.blurb: Its ears are the largest of any canid relative to body size, at close to a third of its body length.

pool.name: Ferret
pool.blurb: Ferrets are fully domesticated descendants of the European polecat, bred by humans for at least 2,500 years - initially for hunting rabbits (a practice called ferreting).

pool.name: Fire Skink
pool.blurb: The fire skink is a West African forest lizard with some of the most striking coloring of any commonly kept reptile: brilliant red flanks broken by black and silver barring, a gold and bronze back, and a black-and-white banded throat.

pool.name: Southern Flying Squirrel
pool.blurb: The Southern flying squirrel is a small nocturnal rodent native to the deciduous forests of eastern North America, gliding between trees on a furred membrane called a patagium stretched between its wrists and ankles.

pool.name: French Bulldog
pool.blurb: The French bulldog was developed in Paris in the mid-1800s by crossing English bulldogs brought by lace workers migrating to France with local Parisian dogs.

pool.name: Gaboon Viper
pool.blurb: It holds on after biting rather than striking and releasing, which is unusual for a viper.

pool.name: Gargoyle Gecko
pool.blurb: Endemic to southern New Caledonia, the gargoyle gecko takes its name from the bumpy protrusions on its head that resemble stone gargoyles.

pool.name: Garter Snake
pool.blurb: The common garter snake is one of the most widely distributed reptiles in North America, found in gardens, wetlands, and vacant lots from Florida to coastal Quebec and west to British Columbia - genuinely one of the most common "found in the backyard" snakes in the US.

pool.name: Crested Gecko
pool.blurb: Native to New Caledonia's southern islands, the crested gecko was thought extinct until rediscovered in 1994.

pool.name: Gerbil
pool.blurb: The Mongolian gerbil comes from the steppe and semi-desert of Mongolia and northern China, and it is built to lose as little water as possible: it concentrates its urine heavily, produces almost no odor, and can go a remarkably long time on the moisture in its food.

pool.name: German Shepherd
pool.blurb: The German shepherd was developed in late 19th-century Germany by cavalry captain Max von Stephanitz, who sought to create the ideal herding and working dog through selective breeding.

pool.name: Ghost Shrimp
pool.blurb: Ghost shrimp are small, nearly transparent freshwater shrimp from the genus Palaemon (long listed under the older genus name Palaemonetes), sold under names like ghost shrimp and glass shrimp, with lookalikes such as whisker shrimp sometimes mislabeled under the same name.

pool.name: Giraffe
pool.blurb: The 25 pound heart figure traces to a single 1955 paper that was already contradicted and went unchecked for decades.

pool.name: Glass Frog
pool.blurb: While sleeping, some glass frogs move almost all their red blood cells into the liver, which makes them close to twice as transparent.

pool.name: Golden Retriever
pool.blurb: Golden retrievers were developed in Scotland in the mid-19th century by crossing flat-coated retrievers with Tweed water spaniels and other breeds to create an ideal hunting dog for Scotland's rugged terrain.

pool.name: Goldfish
pool.blurb: The goldfish is one of the earliest domesticated fish, bred in China over a thousand years ago from a wild silver-gray carp relative for its color mutations.

pool.name: Guinea Pig
pool.blurb: Guinea pigs (cavies) have never been found in the wild - they are a fully domesticated species descended from South American wild cavies, selectively bred by Andean peoples for over 3,000 years as a food source and in religious ceremonies.

pool.name: Guppy
pool.blurb: The guppy is a small, prolific livebearing fish native to the streams and rivers of northeastern South America and the Caribbean.

pool.name: Hamster
pool.blurb: The Syrian hamster - the most common pet hamster species - was first brought into captivity from a single wild-caught female found near Aleppo, Syria in 1930; nearly every pet Syrian hamster alive today descends from that one litter.

pool.name: Hedgehog
pool.blurb: The African pygmy hedgehog - the species most commonly kept as a pet - is native to the arid savanna and grassland of central Africa.

pool.name: Hermit Crab
pool.blurb: The Caribbean hermit crab, also called the purple pincer hermit crab, is the most commonly kept pet land hermit crab, native to coastal regions of the Caribbean and the western Atlantic.

pool.name: Hognose Snake
pool.blurb: Hognose snakes are famous for their dramatic bluffing behavior - they hiss loudly, flatten their heads cobra-like, and if that fails, roll over and play dead convincingly (complete with open mouth and lolling tongue).

pool.name: Honey Badger
pool.blurb: Its venom resistance comes from the same kind of receptor change that protects the mongoose.

pool.name: Humpback Whale
pool.blurb: Researchers identify individuals from tail fluke markings the way you would use a fingerprint.

pool.name: Siberian Husky
pool.blurb: Siberian huskies were bred by the Chukchi people of northeastern Siberia over thousands of years as endurance sled dogs capable of running 100+ miles per day in sub-zero conditions on minimal food.

pool.name: Green Iguana
pool.blurb: Green iguanas are large arboreal herbivores from Central and South America, and the gap between what they are sold as and what they become is the widest of any pet reptile.

pool.name: Immortal Jellyfish
pool.blurb: The reversal is called transdifferentiation, and cells switching type this cleanly is rare enough that cancer researchers pay attention.

pool.name: Jumping Spider
pool.blurb: The regal jumping spider is the most commonly kept pet jumping spider, native to scrubland, palmetto stands, and forest edges of the southeastern United States and the Caribbean.

pool.name: California Kingsnake
pool.blurb: The California kingsnake is a non-venomous colubrid found throughout the western United States and northwestern Mexico.

pool.name: Koi
pool.blurb: Koi are ornamental varieties of the Amur carp, developed in Japan starting in the early 19th century from food carp that displayed unusual color mutations.

pool.name: Labrador Retriever
pool.blurb: The Labrador retriever held the AKC number one spot for 31 straight years until the French Bulldog overtook it in 2022, and it still ranks number 2.

pool.name: Leafy Sea Dragon
pool.blurb: Unlike seahorses it cannot grip with its tail, so a storm can carry one a long way.

pool.name: Leopard Gecko
pool.blurb: Found across arid regions from Pakistan to northwestern India, leopard geckos are ground-dwelling lizards that shelter in rocky outcrops and dry grasslands by day.

pool.name: Lion
pool.blurb: Lionesses in a pride often give birth around the same time and raise the cubs as one group.

pool.name: Lovebird
pool.blurb: Lovebirds are a genus of nine small parrot species native to Africa and Madagascar.

pool.name: Maine Coon
pool.blurb: The Maine Coon is North America's only native longhaired cat breed and one of the oldest natural breeds on the continent, believed to have descended from longhaired cats brought by Viking explorers or New England seafarers.

pool.name: Giant Manta Ray
pool.blurb: Every manta has a unique belly spot pattern, so researchers identify individuals by photograph.

pool.name: Praying Mantis
pool.blurb: Praying mantises are ambush predators in the order Mantodea, with over 2,400 species found across tropical and temperate regions worldwide.

pool.name: Mantis Shrimp
pool.blurb: The strike is so fast the water beside the club vaporises, and the collapsing bubble lands a second hit.

pool.name: Milk Snake
pool.blurb: Milk snakes are a widely distributed kingsnake species found from Canada through Central America.

pool.name: Giant African Millipede
pool.blurb: The giant African millipede is one of the largest millipede species on Earth, native to the subtropical and tropical forests of East Africa.

pool.name: Molly
pool.blurb: Mollies are prolific livebearing fish native to fresh and brackish waters of the southern United States, Mexico, and Central America, closely related to guppies and platies.

pool.name: Mourning Gecko
pool.blurb: The mourning gecko holds a remarkable distinction: wild populations are almost entirely female and reproduce through parthenogenesis - producing fertile eggs without fertilization.

pool.name: Fancy Mouse
pool.blurb: The fancy mouse is a domesticated form of the house mouse, bred for coat color and pattern since at least Victorian England, where Walter Maxey founded the National Mouse Club in 1895 and designed the standard show cage still used today.

pool.name: Narwhal
pool.blurb: A very small number of narwhals grow two tusks.

pool.name: Neon Tetra
pool.blurb: The neon tetra is a small, brightly colored schooling fish native to the clearwater and blackwater streams of the western Amazon Basin.

pool.name: Octopus
pool.blurb: It is very likely color-blind, which makes its color-matching camouflage a genuinely open question.

pool.name: Oscar
pool.blurb: The oscar is a large, predatory cichlid native to the Amazon Basin, prized in the aquarium hobby for its intelligence and strong bonds with individual keepers - behavior distinctive enough to have earned it the nickname 'water dog.' Oscars are naturally curious and active diggers, regularly rearranging substrate and decor in their environment.

pool.name: Pacman Frog
pool.blurb: The ornate horned frog - nicknamed the Pacman frog for its enormous, round, gaping mouth - is native to the grasslands and rainforests of South America.

pool.name: Pangolin
pool.blurb: The scales are keratin, the same material as human fingernails and rhino horn, and have no proven medicinal value.

pool.name: Panther Chameleon
pool.blurb: Males from different valleys look so different that keepers name them by locale, like Ambilobe or Nosy Be.

pool.name: Parrotlet
pool.blurb: The Pacific parrotlet is the most popular of the nine parrotlet species and, at well under six inches, the smallest true parrot commonly kept as a pet - smaller even than a budgie.

pool.name: Emperor Penguin
pool.blurb: Mating for life is largely a myth here; the great majority of pairs re-pair the next season.

pool.name: Persian
pool.blurb: Persians are one of the oldest recognized cat breeds, with a history tracing to the 1600s when longhaired cats from Persia (modern Iran) and Turkey were brought to Europe.

pool.name: Platy
pool.blurb: The platy is a small, exceptionally hardy livebearer native to the Atlantic-slope river systems of Mexico, Belize, and Guatemala.

pool.name: Platypus
pool.blurb: It closes its eyes, ears and nostrils underwater and finds prey purely by electric field.

pool.name: Bristlenose Pleco
pool.blurb: The bristlenose pleco is a small, hardy, algae-grazing armored catfish native to South America.

pool.name: Praying Mantis
pool.blurb: Praying mantises are ambush predators in the order Mantodea, with over 2,400 species found across tropical and temperate regions worldwide.

pool.name: Quaker Parakeet
pool.blurb: Also called the monk parakeet, this is the only parrot in the world that builds its own stick nest rather than using a tree hollow.

pool.name: Rabbit
pool.blurb: The European rabbit is the ancestor of all domestic rabbit breeds - over 300 recognized worldwide.

pool.name: Ragdoll
pool.blurb: The ragdoll is a large, semi-longhaired breed developed in California in the 1960s by breeder Ann Baker, who selectively bred for an extremely docile temperament.

pool.name: Fancy Rat
pool.blurb: Fancy rats are the domesticated form of the wild brown rat, bred for temperament and color since Victorian England, most famously by Jack Black, Queen Victoria's official rat catcher, who caught and bred unusually colored rats and sold them to the wealthy as pets in the 1800s.

pool.name: Golden Retriever
pool.blurb: Golden retrievers were developed in Scotland in the mid-19th century by crossing flat-coated retrievers with Tweed water spaniels and other breeds to create an ideal hunting dog for Scotland's rugged terrain.

pool.name: Rhinoceros
pool.blurb: Rhino horn has the same composition as your fingernails, which is worth remembering given what it sells for.

pool.name: Rosy Boa
pool.blurb: The rosy boa is a small, desert-dwelling boa native to the arid Southwestern United States and Baja California, Mexico - a striking contrast to the Boa constrictor, which can grow six to ten times longer.

pool.name: Rottweiler
pool.blurb: The Rottweiler descends from Roman drover dogs bred to move and guard the herds that fed the legions.

pool.name: Russian Tortoise
pool.blurb: The Russian tortoise (also called Horsfield's tortoise) is a compact, hardy species native to the arid steppes and rocky desert from Kazakhstan to Pakistan and China.

pool.name: Tiger Salamander
pool.blurb: The tiger salamander is the largest land-dwelling salamander in North America, found across a vast range from Canada to Mexico.

pool.name: Savannah Monitor
pool.blurb: The savannah monitor is a medium-to-large monitor lizard native to the sub-Saharan African savanna and semi-arid grasslands.

pool.name: Emperor Scorpion
pool.blurb: The emperor scorpion is one of the largest scorpion species in the world and the most widely kept scorpion as a pet.

pool.name: Scottish Fold
pool.blurb: The Scottish Fold began in 1961 when a shepherd found a folded-ear cat named Susie on a farm in the Tayside region of Scotland.

pool.name: Sea Otter
pool.blurb: A sea otter eats about a quarter of its own body weight every day.

pool.name: Leafy Sea Dragon
pool.blurb: Unlike seahorses it cannot grip with its tail, so a storm can carry one a long way.

pool.name: Seahorse
pool.blurb: The pouch is not a bag he carries. It regulates salinity and delivers oxygen, and the birth is genuine labor.

pool.name: Serval
pool.blurb: Its ears are large enough to hear rodents moving underground and in thick grass, and it will hunt with its eyes closed to concentrate on the sound.

pool.name: Sharks
pool.blurb: Shark skin is covered in dermal denticles, structurally teeth, which is why older accounts describe it as sandpaper.

pool.name: German Shepherd
pool.blurb: The German shepherd was developed in late 19th-century Germany by cavalry captain Max von Stephanitz, who sought to create the ideal herding and working dog through selective breeding.

pool.name: Shima Enaga
pool.blurb: Its diet is almost entirely insects and their eggs and larvae, especially moth and butterfly eggs, even in the depths of a Hokkaido winter.

pool.name: Shoebill
pool.blurb: Its main display is a rapid bill clattering that sounds mechanical rather than birdlike.

pool.name: Siamese
pool.blurb: The Siamese is one of the oldest and most recognized cat breeds in the world, originating in Thailand (formerly Siam) where they were treasured by royalty.

pool.name: Three-Toed Sloth
pool.blurb: The weekly descent accounts for a large share of all sloth predation deaths.

pool.name: Slow Loris
pool.blurb: A mother licks venom into her infant’s fur before leaving it parked on a branch.

pool.name: Sphynx
pool.blurb: The Sphynx traces to a spontaneous mutation in 1966, when a domestic cat in Toronto gave birth to a hairless kitten.

pool.name: Jumping Spider
pool.blurb: The regal jumping spider is the most commonly kept pet jumping spider, native to scrubland, palmetto stands, and forest edges of the southeastern United States and the Caribbean.

pool.name: Southern Flying Squirrel
pool.blurb: The Southern flying squirrel is a small nocturnal rodent native to the deciduous forests of eastern North America, gliding between trees on a furred membrane called a patagium stretched between its wrists and ankles.

pool.name: Stick Insect
pool.blurb: Stick insects (phasmatids) are the world's greatest masters of camouflage, with over 3,000 species evolved to mimic twigs, leaves, and bark with remarkable precision.

pool.name: Sugar Glider
pool.blurb: Sugar gliders are small marsupials native to Australia, New Guinea, and eastern Indonesia - more closely related to koalas and kangaroos than to flying squirrels, which they superficially resemble.

pool.name: Sulcata Tortoise
pool.blurb: The sulcata tortoise - also known as the African spurred tortoise - is the third-largest tortoise species on Earth.

pool.name: Swordtail
pool.blurb: The swordtail is a livebearer native to the Atlantic-slope rivers of Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, and Honduras, and one of the platy's closest relatives, sharing the genus Xiphophorus, Greek for 'sword bearer.' Males grow a long, colorful lower extension of the tail fin, the namesake 'sword,' that plays no role in swimming but is a genuine target of female mate choice, with females showing measurable preferences for males with longer swords and bolder patterning.

pool.name: Tarantula
pool.blurb: Tarantulas are the largest spiders on Earth, with over 900 recognized species found on every continent except Antarctica.

pool.name: Argentine Black and White Tegu
pool.blurb: The Argentine black and white tegu is one of the largest lizards in South America, with intelligence rivaling that of monitor lizards.

pool.name: Thorny Devil
pool.blurb: It can draw water from wet sand without ever lowering its head to drink.

pool.name: Tiger
pool.blurb: Shave a tiger and the stripes are still there, because the pattern is in the skin.

pool.name: Tiger Salamander
pool.blurb: The tiger salamander is the largest land-dwelling salamander in North America, found across a vast range from Canada to Mexico.

pool.name: Tokay Gecko
pool.blurb: The tokay gecko is one of the largest gecko species, named for its distinctive "to-kay!" mating call audible from considerable distance.

pool.name: Russian Tortoise
pool.blurb: The Russian tortoise (also called Horsfield's tortoise) is a compact, hardy species native to the arid steppes and rocky desert from Kazakhstan to Pakistan and China.

pool.name: White's Tree Frog
pool.blurb: White's tree frog - also called the dumpy tree frog or Australian green tree frog - is a large, robust arboreal frog native to Australia and southern New Guinea.

pool.name: Uromastyx
pool.blurb: Uromastyx, also called spiny-tailed lizards or dabb lizards, are robust, herbivorous lizards native to rocky desert and arid landscapes stretching from North Africa to the Middle East and South Asia.

pool.name: Veiled Chameleon
pool.blurb: The veiled chameleon is native to the mountainous valleys of Yemen and southwestern Saudi Arabia, where it tolerates wider swings in temperature and humidity than most other chameleon species - an adaptation to its relatively dry, variable habitat.

pool.name: Humpback Whale
pool.blurb: Researchers identify individuals from tail fluke markings the way you would use a fingerprint.

pool.name: Gray Wolf
pool.blurb: The researcher most responsible for the alpha idea asked his own publisher to stop reprinting the book.

pool.name: Wolverine
pool.blurb: The species name Gulo gulo means glutton twice over.

pool.name: Wombat
pool.blurb: Cubes do not roll off the rocks and logs a wombat uses as scent posts, which appears to be the point.

pool.name: Zebra Danio
pool.blurb: The zebra danio is a small, fast-swimming schooling fish native to the shallow streams, ditches, and monsoon-flooded rice paddies of South Asia.

pool.name: Zebra Finch
pool.blurb: The zebra finch is one of the most popular pet birds in the world and, alongside the canary, one of the few non-parrot birds kept as a pet - it is a true finch, and its care reflects that: no talking, no hand-taming the way a parrot bonds with an owner, and a strong instinct to live in flocks rather than pair off with a person.
